== Biography ==
'''James Glasgow''' was recorded at Killycarragh, County Tyrone, in the Public Record Office of Northern Ireland's index of pre-1858 wills and administrations. The entry is indexed under 21 March 1836.<ref name="Killycarragh1836">Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, [https://apps.proni.gov.uk/ProniNames_IE/SearchPage.aspx PRONI Names], ''Pre-1858 Wills and Admons'', search result for James Glasgow, Killycarragh, 21 March 1836, accessed 7 September 2026. The result's item-detail URL is session-bound and the original probate document does not survive.</ref>

The index date should not be treated as an exact death date. The entry establishes a probate subject named James Glasgow and his recorded residence, but it supplies no age, occupation or relatives.<ref name="Killycarragh1836" />

A later family statement preserved as PRONI T1959/3 describes the writer's paternal grandfather, William Glasgow of Killycurragh, as the husband of an unidentified Miss Cunningham of Omagh and father of five sons and three daughters. The writer said that her father and a brother William were educated together; William became a physician in England. Three other sons—apparently Henry, James and Samuel—“lived and died on [the] farm in Killycurragh,” with Samuel remaining in their parents' house.<ref name="T1959">Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, T1959/3, photocopy of an undated and unsigned Glasgow–Rutherford family letter preserved with papers of the 1890s; online transcription by Albert Rutherford reproduced by Gary Harding, [https://www.genealogy.com/forum/surnames/topics/rutherford/5445/ “Rutherfords and Glasgows in Co. Tyrone, Ireland”], 9 January 2005.</ref>

That relationship-defined James is the strongest and probable identity for the same-named Killycarragh probate subject. The letter's writer was born five months after her father, Rev. John Glasgow of Orritor, died in July 1801, placing the named James in the correct generation.<ref name="T1959" /> A Presbyterian-ministers compilation independently identifies John Glasgow of Orritor as the minister ordained at New Row, Coleraine, on 8 March 1796 and records his death on 13 July 1801.<ref name="RevJohn">[https://cotyrone.com/churchrecord/ministers-pres.html “Presbyterian Ministers in Co. Tyrone”], entry for John Glasgow of Orritor and New Row, Coleraine, citing his ordination on 8 March 1796 and death on 13 July 1801.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Killycurragh generations, 20 October 2026 ===

The freshly read published transcription of PRONI T1959/3 distinguishes an older William of Killycurragh, the writer’s paternal great-grandfather, from his son William, the writer’s paternal grandfather and husband of Miss Cunningham. The younger William is the Cunningham husband, whose sons included James and Samuel. His son John married Margaret Glasgow after ordination at Coleraine and died at his father’s house in Orritor in July 1801. The surviving child, the anonymous writer, was born five months later; Margaret died in 1817. The separate church compilation identifies John Glasgow from Orritor, ordained at New Row, Coleraine, on 8 March 1796 and dead on 13 July 1801. The shared ministry, origin, name and death month strongly identify the husband. The writer separately describes Margaret’s father William as a son of James Glasgow and Margaret Rutherford; the two parental lines must not be collapsed into one grandfather.

Select [[Glasgow-1318|William Glasgow]] as the possible father of the letter-defined Cunningham husband at 36%. The letter supplies an older Killycurragh William, son of the Tullycoll/Tullyall William and brother of James (husband of Margaret Rutherford) and John (husband of Anne Mason). The 1705 Kirknewton child William has a named father William and a generation compatible with being grandfather of the minister ordained in 1796. The 1702 John baptism supplies a compatible second named son in that Scottish father cluster; the existing James-1025 family supplies the Irish James comparison. This is a positive but non-exclusive family-cluster hypothesis. The Scottish child’s adult identity and migration remain unproved. The 36% includes that identity uncertainty; it is not a confident Scottish–Irish bridge.

Select the letter-defined William of Killycurragh as Rev. John Glasgow’s father at 94% (strongly supported). The writer explicitly gives the writer’s father John, the writer’s paternal grandfather William and his Cunningham marriage. John’s Coleraine ordination, Orritor origin and July 1801 death match the separate New Row minister entry. This concerns the minister’s record-defined identity; it does not identify his grandfather with a Scottish baptism or upgrade his brothers’ later-profile matches.

Select [[Glasgow-2426|William Glasgow]] as Margaret Glasgow’s probable father at 84%. That profile represents William, son of [[Glasgow-1025|James Glasgow]] and Margaret Rutherford, which matches the letter’s maternal-grandfather family position. The letter explicitly names the eldest daughter Margaret as the minister’s wife and the writer’s mother. The profile’s circa-1735 birth and circa-1829 United States death are inherited claims, not exclusionary records and not corrected here. The letter calls William an eldest son; the circa-1735 estimate conflicts with the earlier estimated births of his attached brothers. Those unverified estimates require checking and are preserved here. This is the maternal grandfather, distinct from the Cunningham husband. Original records and an independent adult-life bridge remain to be found.

These are exact subjective assessments of complete relationship-and-identity propositions, not measured probabilities. The family letter is undated and unsigned and is read through Albert Rutherford’s published transcription of a photocopy, not an inspected PRONI original. The minister list is a derivative compilation whose independence from the family tradition is unproved. The Scottish adult identities remain possible: neither the letter nor the 1705 baptism supplies a migration, occupation, property or witness bridge between Kirknewton and Tyrone. The letter’s three-son family and second-cousin statement are internally consistent clues from one source, not independent corroborations. Existing people, vital fields and mothers are preserved. Miss Cunningham and Anne Rutherford are reported maternal names, not transferred to existing maternal profiles. The letter’s first-settler story is family tradition, not proof of the first Glasgow in Tyrone or of the surname’s origin.<ref name="KillycurraghGenerations20261020">PRONI T1959/3, [https://www.genealogy.com/forum/surnames/topics/rutherford/5445/ published transcription], read 20 October 2026; original uninspected. [https://cotyrone.com/churchrecord/ministers-pres.html Minister compilation], John Glasgow, New Row; derivative entry, not an original register.</ref>

=== Working father review, 20 October 2026 ===

Prefer the William named in PRONI T1959/3 as James Glasgow-4145’s probable working father, at 82% confidence. The letter’s paternal uncle James lived and died on the Killycurragh farm, matching the name, specific locality, generation and deceased status of the probate subject indexed at Killycarragh on 21 March 1836. The letter supplies the parent relationship absent from that index. The whole match remains inferred because the original probate document is lost and the letter is derivative; another local James remains possible.

The percentages assess each entire father-to-profile proposition, including identification of the named son with the later profile; they are subjective comparative judgments, not measured frequencies. The original letter and holding succession remain unverified. Samuel’s circa-1800 birth is an estimate, and a materially older Samuel or a later same-name descendant is possible. His wife Anne’s approximate 1801 birth and their children in the 1820s–1830s do not date Samuel himself. A nephew or later tenant could share the name and townland. Do not transfer a recorded relationship to a later adult merely from the letter’s parent clause. William’s birth and death remain unknown. The letter names an older William as his father; the specific Kirknewton profile is a 36% possibility. His mother remains unidentified. Miss Cunningham is retained as William’s reported wife, without selecting her as either profile’s mother. No existing person is merged or redated, and no live WikiTree edit has been made.

Inspect PRONI T1959/3 and associated family papers; test William’s identity against existing candidates and trace the Killycurragh holding through leases, rentals and valuation revisions. Establish Samuel’s age independently. The 1836 index date is probate information, not James’s exact death date.<ref>PRONI T1959/3; [https://www.genealogy.com/forum/surnames/topics/rutherford/5445/ published family-letter transcription], earlier reviewed account reused; original not newly inspected. [https://glasgow.phenotype.dev/people/record-william-glasgow-killycurragh-t1959.html Sourced William Glasgow draft and identity comparisons].</ref>


The index spells the residence ''Killycarragh''. It is probably the townland now rendered Killycurragh in the Oritor electoral division and Derryloran parish. The T1959/3 statement independently places the writer's uncle James on the family farm at Killycurragh and says that he died there. The combined name, place, generation and death evidence supports one probable identity, although the original probate document is lost and the family letter is known only through an online transcription.

The St Luran register records a James Glasgow living at Orritor Craigs in 1829, when a child was baptised to him and Mary Anne of Drumcann.<ref name="Derryloran1829">Representative Church Body Library, [https://www.churchofireland.org/cmsfiles/pdf/AboutUs/library/AngRecord/DerryloranVol1.pdf ''Derryloran Parish Register, Volume 1''], baptism no. 466, 5 April 1829.</ref> He is a useful locality candidate for the 1836 estate, but the shared forename and neighbouring residence do not prove that the two records concern the same person.

=== Duplicate audit ===

The duplicate audit below predates creation of this existing Glasgow-4145 profile. It is retained as research history; do not create this person again. The current 82% working father assessment above supersedes the former blanket attachment hold.

The local One Tree export and live WikiTree data were searched again in September 2026. The strongest automated place-name result is demonstrably not the deceased man:

* [[Glasgow-1701|James Glasgow junior]] lived at Killycurragh but died there on 27 July 1875. His exact-place match is valuable for local context, not identity with the 1836 probate subject.
* [[Glasgow-1702|James Glasgow of Ballynasollus]] died in 1882 and cannot be this man.
* [[Glasgow-3444|James Glasgow of Cookstown]] died in 1866 and cannot be this man.
* [[Glasgow-1165|James Glasgow]] belongs to the separately documented family of John Glasgow and Mary Arthur. His family Bible records his death on 20 April 1823 and gives no Killycurragh connection. The earlier death alone would not exclude a delayed probate entry, but the incompatible relationship-defined family does.
* [[Glasgow-2989|James Glasgow of Derryloran]] is an older local candidate whose death is unresolved, but no source on the profile places him at Killycarragh or identifies him through relatives or property.

No current WikiTree profile is proved to represent this 1836 estate. The surviving index is too slight to show whether the subject was the 1829 Orritor Craigs householder, the older unresolved Derryloran man, or another member of the several contemporary Glasgow households.

The new family discriminator resolves the creation question even though it does not prove an exact birth date. None of the searched profiles represents the son of William Glasgow of Killycurragh and Miss Cunningham who lived and died on the family farm. [[Glasgow-2989|James of Derryloran]] is an older, relationship-free reconstruction, while the exact-place [[Glasgow-1701|James]] lived until 1875. Creating this man unconnected, with the probable family placement in Research Notes, avoids both conflation and omission.

[[Glasgow-1698|Samuel Glasgow]], born about 1800 and reported to have died at
Killycurragh in 1857, is the strongest live candidate for the brother Samuel
whom T1959/3 says remained in his parents' Killycurragh house. This is a useful
probable sibling identity, not proof of a shared parent attachment. By contrast,
[[Glasgow-1675|William Glasgow of Killycurragh]] became a Presbyterian elder and
emigrated to Ohio; that documented life does not fit the letter's physician
William who practised in London and Hull.

=== Further research ===

Inspect the original T1959/3 photocopy, the rest of <code>T1959/1-8</code>, <code>D1413/3a-b</code> and <code>T1762</code>, then trace the Killycurragh holding through Derryloran rentals, deeds and valuation material. Those records may supply James's dates, heirs and his mother's forename. They are still required before making structured parent or sibling attachments, but not before creating the distinct record bearer.
